      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/16/heating-oil-price-increase-winter</link>
      <description><p>Surge in prices is forcing many to cut back on spending, with a projected 21% increase in costs of those households</p><p>Millions of homeowners in the US will pay hundreds of dollars more this winter to heat their homes as rising energy prices have pushed up the price of heating oil.</p><p>The US Energy Information Administration <a href="https://www.eia.gov/todayinenergy/detail.php?id=68264&amp;utm_medium=email">projects</a> households that use heating oil can expect to pay 21% more this year compared with last winter, with warmer temperatures expected to partly offset price increases.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/16/heating-oil-price-increase-winter">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/16/companies-trump-tariff-refunds-corporate-bonuses</link>
      <description><p>Some firms are directing refunds to corporate leadership instead of reimbursing consumers, ProPublica finds </p><p>Several companies that received refunds for paying <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/trump-tariffs">tariffs</a> have put those funds towards corporate bonuses instead of reimbursing consumers, <a href="https://www.propublica.org/article/trump-tariff-refunds-corporate-bonuses">an investigation</a> from ProPublica has found.</p><p>After analyzing securities filings and earnings calls, ProPublica identified at least nine companies who said they are receiving tariff refunds and noted they are directing some of those funds to their leadership.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/16/companies-trump-tariff-refunds-corporate-bonuses">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>College students rally in support of Starbucks baristas urging boycott over contract negotiations</title>

      <description><p>Rallies are planned at more than US 40 campuses as workers seeking better pay and conditions decry stalled talks</p><p>Starbucks baristas, students, elected officials and allies are planning rallies at <a href="https://starbucksworkersunited.controlshift.app/events?link_id=2&amp;can_id=debd8d2ad19f005d15f9bbdff314d42a&amp;source=email-nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;email_referrer=email_3490793&amp;email_subject=nov-12-day-of-action-for-starbucks-baristas&amp;&amp;">over 40 college campuses</a> across the US on Thursday to support the Starbucks Workers United <a href="https://www.boycottstarbucks.net/">boycott campaign</a> as the union nears five years of deadlock with the company over contract negotiations.</p><p>Starbucks Workers United is <a href="https://sbworkersunited.org/what-were-fighting-for-updates-on-contract-bargaining/">seeking</a> better pay and stronger staffing levels, including a $17 an hour minimum wage for baristas and a minimum staffing of three workers per store.
